# Prerequisites

Please have the following ready before class:

* Have your OSCER credentials on hand
* Be able to access your OSCER account through Terminal or MobaXterm
  - If you are on a Windows machine, please make sure to have MobaXterm installed

# Learning objectives

At the end of this lesson you will:

* Learn to log into your OSCER account
* Be more familiar with using BASH and navigating OSCER through the terminal
* Have submitted your first SBATCH script

# Lecture Slides

![](../slides/lecture2_oscer_bash.pdf){width=800px height=480px}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Exercise #1" appearance="simple"}
```{.bash}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=normal
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --mem=1G
#SBATCH --job-name=jobname
#SBATCH --output=jobname_%J_%A_%a_stdout.txt
#SBATCH --error=jobname_%J_%A_%a_stderr.txt
#SBATCH --time=0:10:00
#SBATCH --mail-user=EMAIL@ou.edu
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL
#SBATCH --chdir=/scratch/USER/lecture_2

#==============================================================================
# BASH Strict mode (i.e. "fail fast" to reduce hard-to-find bugs)
set -e          # EXIT the script if any command returns non-zero exit status.
set -E          # Make ERR trapping work inside functions too.
set -u          # Variables must be pre-defined before using them.
set -o pipefail  # If a pipe fails, returns the error code for the failed pipe
                #  even if it isn't the last command in a series of pipes.
#==============================================================================

echo "Hello World!" > helloWorld.txt
```
:::
